subject: Qualification recap — model selection pathways & eval plan
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@ledgerly.com>, contracts@ledgerly.com
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Qualification recap — model selection pathways & eval plan

Hi Samir — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and proposal of next steps so we all have the same view.

Call highlights (30 min):
- Primary goal: replace Ledgerly’s current proprietary summary model for transaction narratives with an open-model candidate that matches or exceeds your precision on the legal/finance prompts.
- Key non-negotiables: PII redaction consistency, deterministic behavior for audit logs, and <=200ms tail latency for single-record summaries under our dedicated offering.
- Current baseline: Ledgerly-prop-v2 (internal metrics): QA pass 86% on your sample, F1 on entity extraction 0.84.

Proposal (concrete):
1) Run a 2-week parity validation comparing two open candidates (Llama-3-Chat-16k-quant and Mosaic-14B-q8) vs your proprietary baseline (Ledgerly-prop-v2).
   - Acceptance criteria: match-or-beat on 우리 business-critical metrics — QA pass >= 88% OR entity-extraction F1 >= 0.86, and no downstream parsed-field-breaks > 3% (see definitions in attached spreadsheet).
2) Evaluation harness: we’ll run 5k representative examples you supplied + 1k hard edge cases. We’ll score: QA pass rate (human labels), EM/F1 for extraction, hallucination incidents (annotated), latency P50/P95.
3) Prompt/perf strategy: supply canonical prompt bundles (attached: benchmark_prompts_v1.jsonl). We’ll test both few-shot and system-prompt variants, plus small truncation/temperature sweeps.
4) Risk mitigations: if an open candidate fails parity but is within 3 points on QA, we can test quantized fine-tuning (adapter) or fallback routing to Ledgerly-prop-v2 for sensitive flows.

Next steps I suggest (owners & timeline):
- Today: I’ll upload the eval harness and initial prompt set (attached). (Owner: me)
- By Tue 5/25: you confirm the 5k sample split + sign the NDA amendment for sharing the full audit traces (Owner: Samir / contracts).
- Wed 5/26: we kick automated runs and share preliminary metrics by Fri 5/28.

Attachments: benchmark_prompts_v1.jsonl (prompt sets), ledgerly_parity_proposal.xlsx (acceptance criteria & scoring rubrics).

Open questions I flagged on the call:
- Are the parsed-field requirements (currency normalizations, date canonicalization) strict or negotiable?
- Which users/roles require explicit redaction logs in plain text vs. hashed IDs?

Thanks — I’ll stand up the harness as soon as you confirm the splits.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
[Attachment: benchmark_prompts_v1.jsonl (jsonl)]
[Attachment: ledgerly_parity_proposal.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@ledgerly.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, contracts@ledgerly.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Qualification recap — model selection pathways & eval plan

Thanks Neha — this is very clear and appreciated. A few quick answers: 
- Parsed-field requirements are strict for finance/legal flows; we need canonical currency and ISO dates. Small normalization exceptions possible but must be documented.
- Redaction: we need both hashed IDs (for downstream joins) and a short plaintext redaction audit for compliance reviewers (redacted tokens list).

We’ll confirm the 5k split by Monday EOD. Contracts: I’ll have our legal ops review the NDA amendment and loop in contracts@ledgerly.com.

One ask: can you also capture exact prompt + model checkpoint versions in the report (we need reproducibility for audits)?

—Samir
Samir Rao
Head of ML & Data Products | Ledgerly
samir.rao@ledgerly.com
[Company: Ledgerly]

Thanks Samir — yes, reproducibility is part of the plan. We’ll capture model checkpoint IDs, tokenization configs, and the exact prompt text + system messages in the audit CSV.

Small clarification on acceptance gates: I proposed an OR between QA pass rate and extraction F1 because some open models show better high-level QA even if extraction lags slightly. If Ledgerly prefers a strict AND, we can update the rubric — say so in your reply.

Operational note: for the latency SLOs, the dedicated pool we demo will report P50/P95 and we can set a canary route that falls back to Ledgerly-prop-v2 if P95 > 400ms on any nightly run.

I’ll start the initial injection run on Wed (5/26) once you confirm splits.

Best,
Neha

Quick internal note — two technical asks from my side before we kick runs: 
1) Please include a small 200-example labeled holdout that exercises rare corner cases (multicurrency, nested parentheses in narratives). We should keep that separate from the 5k so it can be used for sanity QA.
2) I’ll prepare a minimal inference config for both Llama-3-Chat-16k-quant and Mosaic-14B-q8 (batch sizes, kv-cache settings, quantization flags) so the bench is apples-to-apples.

I’ll share the configs by Monday morning.
